findings.body: Every removal performs a delegate getByAlias query before consulting the cached alias entry, adding a database round trip to the common cache-hit path that previously needed none.
findings.failure_mode: The cache-backed removal path loses its cache-hit performance benefit and issues avoidable SQL.
findings.impact: Every removal performs a delegate getByAlias query before consulting the cached alias entry, adding a database round trip to the common cache-hit path that previously needed none.
findings.root_cause: The delegate lookup was moved ahead of the cache lookup and is executed unconditionally.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the cached identity-provider model for login invalidation when the alias cache entry exists, and call idpDelegate.getByAlias only for invalid or missing cache entries.
findings.title: Removal now performs an unnecessary database lookup on cache hits
findings.trigger: Remove an identity provider whose alias entry is already present and valid in the Infinispan cache.
findings.verifier_reason: Line R100 shows 'IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);' is now called unconditionally before the isInvalid check at R101. Previously (L92), the delegate lookup only happened inside the isInvalid branch. This adds a database query on every remove() call even when cache is valid, which is a performance regression.

findings.body: All twenty cleanup actions attempt to remove a nonexistent provider named "alias" while the created providers remain in the realm, potentially failing teardown and contaminating subsequent tests.
findings.failure_mode: Test fixtures are not removed and cleanup may report repeated not-found failures.
findings.impact: All twenty cleanup actions attempt to remove a nonexistent provider named "alias" while the created providers remain in the realm, potentially failing teardown and contaminating subsequent tests.
findings.root_cause: The cleanup registration uses a hard-coded placeholder string rather than the alias assigned to idpRep.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the generated alias in each iteration and register cleanup for testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias).remove().
findings.title: Loop cleanup targets the literal alias instead of the created providers
findings.trigger: testCacheIDPForLogin finishes after creating identity providers idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19 and its registered cleanup actions run.
findings.verifier_reason: Line R381 shows 'getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);' inside a loop that creates providers with aliases 'idp-alias-0' through 'idp-alias-19'. The cleanup uses hardcoded literal 'alias' instead of the actual alias like 'idp-alias-' + i. This will fail to clean up the created providers.

pr.title: Add cache for IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin

raw_findings.body: The subsequent getById inside update can return the same already-mutated cached object, so the helper sees identical "original" and updated states and skips invalidation. A primed getForLogin cache then continues omitting a newly enabled provider or returning a disabled, hidden, or link-only provider.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A membership-changing update is misclassified as preserving login eligibility, leaving the cached ID set stale.
raw_findings.impact: The subsequent getById inside update can return the same already-mutated cached object, so the helper sees identical "original" and updated states and skips invalidation. A primed getForLogin cache then continues omitting a newly enabled provider or returning a disabled, hidden, or link-only provider.
raw_findings.root_cause: The invalidation decision assumes idpById is an immutable pre-update snapshot, although cached identity-provider models can be mutated and passed back to update.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Obtain an independent raw pre-update snapshot from idpDelegate before evaluating changes, or conservatively invalidate every FetchMode login key on update.
raw_findings.title: In-place model updates can bypass login-cache invalidation
raw_findings.trigger: With the organization feature disabled, fetch an identity provider through getById, mutate that returned cached model in place (for example, enable it or set hideOnLogin), and pass the same model to update.

raw_findings.body: The cached original is wrapped so isEnabled() is false solely because the organization is disabled; both predicates can therefore be false and the method skips invalidation even though persistent query membership changed. Re-enabling the organization can expose the now-private, hidden, or link-only provider from the stale cached ID set.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A real transition out of the login query is masked by temporary organization disablement, allowing stale IDs to survive later organization re-enablement.
raw_findings.impact: The cached original is wrapped so isEnabled() is false solely because the organization is disabled; both predicates can therefore be false and the method skips invalidation even though persistent query membership changed. Re-enabling the organization can expose the now-private, hidden, or link-only provider from the stale cached ID set.
raw_findings.root_cause: The helper uses getLoginPredicate on an organization-aware wrapper, whose effective enabled state includes organization status that is not part of the delegate query's cached membership criteria.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Base cache-membership comparisons on raw persisted provider state rather than organization-aware wrappers, or invalidate the login caches unconditionally for identity-provider updates.
raw_findings.title: Organization-aware enabled state can suppress required invalidation
raw_findings.trigger: Prime an organization login cache, disable that organization, and then change one of its enabled public providers to private, hidden, or link-only while leaving its organization association unchanged.

finding.title: In-place model updates can bypass login-cache invalidation
finding.trigger: With the organization feature disabled, fetch an identity provider through getById, mutate that returned cached model in place (for example, enable it or set hideOnLogin), and pass the same model to update.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that getById returns a mutable cached object that can be mutated in place is speculative. CachedIdentityProvider stores an IdentityProviderModel copy (see constructor pattern in similar cache classes). The patch uses getById to obtain the original state before update, which is the standard pattern. No evidence that the cached model is the same mutable instance that callers modify.

finding.root_cause: The helper uses getLoginPredicate on an organization-aware wrapper, whose effective enabled state includes organization status that is not part of the delegate query's cached membership criteria.

finding.title: Organization-aware enabled state can suppress required invalidation
finding.trigger: Prime an organization login cache, disable that organization, and then change one of its enabled public providers to private, hidden, or link-only while leaving its organization association unchanged.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim assumes organization-aware wrapper affects the predicate evaluation incorrectly. However, getLoginPredicate() from LoginFilter checks isEnabled(), isLinkOnly(), isHideOnLogin() and BROKER_PUBLIC config. The organization-aware wrapper only overrides isEnabled() to check org status. The scenario described (org disabled masking a real transition) is speculative - if org is disabled, the IDP wouldn't be in login cache anyway. No concrete evidence this causes stale cache.
